scope: Original62test corpus with common corrected signup helper, one worker, fresh native database/mail/API, unified four-core/8GiB/zero-swap group, private loopback and fresh tmpfs. On-first-retry tracing, no retries or skips. Input hashes outside complete clock. All owned work and sampler overhead inside native command clock.

mappingValidation.source: ELF load segments and exact function symbol ranges, original executable mappings and inherited address-space records; unknown addresses stay unresolved.
mappingValidation.resolution: Actual direct-loaded function pointer and /proc/self/maps bind mapping device/inode to the same hashed library bytes. Retain the different stat device; do not assume those fields are interchangeable.

retainedCorrections.issue: Initial mapping validator assumed perf device equals stat device.
retainedCorrections.resolution: Preserved failure and used an explicit direct-load mapping control before symbol attribution.

retainedCorrections.issue: All Python processes initially labelled as backend bootstrap.
retainedCorrections.resolution: Original recorded owner/observer/API process identities now separate supervision from other Python children; generic other-python stays explicit.

retainedCorrections.issue: Five-millisecond periods miss many short-lived threads.
retainedCorrections.resolution: Retain coarse observations; add one0.5ms profile per engine. No rescaling of missing work into fabricated CPU totals.

retainedCorrections.issue: First denser candidate verifier selected an empty command line observed during exec.
retainedCorrections.resolution: Retain failure; a later original observation with the same PID/start identity contains the full expected argv. Select that record, preserve all original observations, and verify without rerunning the suite.

retainedCorrections.issue: Denser derivative analyzer repeatedly reread its immutable boundary file.
retainedCorrections.resolution: Stop only that analyzer, cache each boundary once and reanalyze original records. No workload or raw capture restarted.

decision.nextTarget: Native Chromium function-level attribution on the primary application workloads; existing custom browser retains an ELF symbol table, so first try the retained binary before considering a rebuild.
decision.rationale: Denser observations show browser processes dominate user-mode samples; the Rust driver contributes a small fraction. Coarse sampling understated short-thread work, including native Argon2. Driver transport rewriting and backend security changes are not selected from this evidence.
decision.speedClaim: None. CPU sample shares are not critical-path wall shares or achievable savings. Most-scenario2x and final release remain open.

limitations: One ordinary control and one5ms sample per framework, followed by one0.5ms sample per framework. No statistical overhead estimate or comparative performance admission.
Task-clock user-mode samples exclude kernel-mode samples and may miss partial periods or short-lived threads. Nominal period sums are estimates, not measured user CPU.
Kernel cgroup CPU includes sampler/supervision costs. The sampler observes its child workload, so these scopes differ; closeness of nominal sums to counters is not a calibration proof.
Roles follow original process identities, executable mappings and fork ancestry. Thread labels alone do not prove semantic roles. Unmapped/JIT addresses and unresolved symbols remain explicit.
Native Argon2 symbol ranges bind to the unchanged sampled library bytes, but no general loaded-memory/transient-change attestation is claimed.
Sampling addresses and CPU do not establish causal critical-path work, per-operation browser ownership or an elapsed-time speedup. Original ordinary timers and backend cryptography remain unchanged.
